card.name: Yalli
card.tagline: Ancient Azerbaijani collective chain dance, UNESCO-listed from Nakhchivan
card.profile: Yalli (Yalli) is an Azerbaijani collective circle/chain/line dance involving games, pantomime (bird and animal imitations) and physical movements, starting slowly and accelerating to near-running speed (UNESCO ICH; Halay, Wikipedia). It is performed hand-in-hand or by finger-grips, traditionally accompanied by zurna and davul (and nagara) (Halay, Wikipedia). Variants include Kochari and Tenzere; 'Yalli (Kochari, Tenzere), traditional group dances of Nakhchivan' was inscribed on 28 November 2018 at the 13th session (13.COM) of UNESCO's Intergovernmental Committee in Port Louis, Mauritius, on Azerbaijan's nomination, on the List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Need of Urgent Safeguarding (UNESCO ICH). It is also danced by Iranian Azerbaijanis in northwestern Iran.
card.insight: Though filed here under Iran, Yalli is fundamentally an Azerbaijani dance, and the UNESCO 2018 listing is Azerbaijan's (Nakhchivan), not Iran's (UNESCO ICH).
card.image_significance: The circle that never breaks. A representative image shows upright carriage, sweeping arm lines and embroidered dress — Nakhchivan/NW Iran, Iran/Azerbaijan.
